triage.note: Cold-reviewer finding T3-3 (tasks/reviews/gates-2026-08-22.json, MEDIUM, reviewer-stated; reproduced by the implementer 2026-08-22 before anything was edited). normalize.py COVER_DATE_RE kept a rigid ',?\s+' between the day and the year, so a cover date typeset without a space after the comma ('December 31,2016') -- or with the comma floated off the day ('December 31 , 2016') -- does not match; and DATE_RE, the regex the captured string is handed to, had the same '\s*,?\s+' demand for at least one space AFTER the comma (the finding credits DATE_RE with already fixing the hazard; it fixes only the floating comma, not the space-less one -- measured, see provenance). period_end comes back None, segment.expected_items' date guard is falsy for every dated code, and the filing is silently demoted to the 14-code 1993 item set with taxonomy_era 'legacy' and doc_status success_with_warning -- the identical failure path caps-cover-taxonomy pins for the all-caps cover, one typesetting choice over. Same class (input-variant): the code is correct for every cover spacing it was tested against; the eval set never contained the other.

This is a real filer typesetting shape, and the tag-stripped iXBRL path can produce it too ('31,2016' loses nothing but may lose the space). MEASURED EFFECT at origin/main 3c2b8f4 (before any fix), the red line: extract_items -> meta.period_end None (unmutated source: 2016-12-31), taxonomy_era 'legacy' (source: 'modern'), 14 items instead of 21, doc_status success_with_warning with the single warning period_end_unknown; the spans bleed by exact arithmetic -- item 1 measures 7,767 chars = 7,496 + 129 (Item 1A) + 142 (Item 1B); item 9 measures 7,454 = 102 + 7,166 (Item 9A) + 186 (Item 9B); item 14 measures 2,624 = 1,253 + 1,371 (Item 15) -- the same three numbers caps-cover-taxonomy records, because it is the same code path. The eval runner's red line: '[FAIL] comma-cover-period' with 11 of 17 checks failing -- warning_absent ("unexpected warning 'period_end_unknown': no period of report found; expected item set is a guess"); item_present 1A/7A/9A/9B/15 ('item 1A not extracted: None' etc.); text_not_contains item 1 ('item 1 contains forbidden 'ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS.'') and item 9 (likewise for 'ITEM 9A(I). CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES'); max_chars 1/9 ('item 1 has 7767 chars > 7600', 'item 9 has 7454 chars > 500'); expected_set_complete ('expected items missing or unstatused: 1A, 1B, 7A, 9A, 9B, 15, 16'). The text_not_contains rows fire here because items 1 and 9 exist and are bled INTO; the max_chars bands beside them are what keeps the assertion load-bearing if a future failure mode drops the item instead (text_not_contains is vacuous on an absent item, as eval_adapter documents). WHY THESE CHECKS: warning_absent(period_end_unknown) is the direct assertion -- the date is on the cover and the pipeline must read it; the item_present, max_chars, text_not_contains, expected_set_complete and only_items rows are copied from caps-cover-taxonomy on purpose: the two fixtures are one-transformation siblings of the same source, so the same 21-item FY2016 inventory is the ground truth for both, and a fix that passes one but not the other has fixed a casing or a spacing rather than the date reader. Both comma shapes are additionally pinned at the layer by normalize.py::_demo (COVER_DATE_RE + _parse_date on 'December 31,2016' and 'December 31 , 2016'), because one fixture can carry only one of them and the floating-comma shape is the one DATE_RE already handled -- so the fixture carries the space-less shape, the one that was red on both regexes. Tagged 'invariant' for the same reason as caps-cover-taxonomy: a silent era demotion produces confident, plausible, wrong spans across the whole document.
